article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet
Breeder: T-Bud of T-Fly Genetics
THC Content: 28%
CBD Content: Low to negligible
Terpene Profile: beta-caryophyllene , myrcene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Creamy orange, grape, berry, sweet sherbet
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Good to potentially heavy
Outdoor Yield: Good
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

2 Scoops takes the dessert theme literally without becoming a strain built around sweetness alone. Grape Sherbet and Orange Sherbet meet in a cannabis hybrid where creamy citrus, dark fruit, earthy funk, and unusually heavy resin production compete for attention. Mature flowers often have the kind of thick trichome coating that gives them an almost glazed appearance, while purple coloration can develop beneath bright orange pistils and pale resin. The fragrance, however, is what originally distinguished the cultivar: an orange-cream aroma reminiscent of old-fashioned frozen push pops followed by a distinctly dank undertone that prevents the profile from becoming sugary or one-dimensional.

The original plant was created in Central California by T-Bud of T-Fly Genetics. Elev8 Seeds later received permission from T-Fly to release the genetics in regular seed form and describes 2 Scoops as one of T-Bud’s most prized creations. Elev8 currently lists the cultivar as Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet, with a nine-week flowering period, good yield, very high potency, and exceptional trichome production. The seed release has since been retired from the company’s active catalog.
Genetics and Lineage

The parentage of 2 Scoops is straightforward: Grape Sherbet crossed with Orange Sherbet. Rather than using dramatically different cannabis families, T-Bud doubled down on complementary Sherbet expressions. Grape Sherbet supplies the darker fruit side of the combination, pushing aromas toward grape, berries, sweetness, and occasionally deeper earthy tones. Orange Sherbet supplies the bright citrus half, adding creamy orange characteristics that can resemble sherbet, orange candy, or an orange-vanilla frozen dessert.

Bringing those two profiles together produced more than a novelty flavor cross. Elev8 emphasizes that the selected 2 Scoops plant stood apart because of the combination of extreme frost and an unusually loud terpene profile. According to the breeder’s current description, T-Bud considered it his “crown jewel” after decades of working with California cannabis genetics, while T-Fly authorized Elev8 to distribute the line as regular seed. That history makes T-Fly Genetics the appropriate original breeder attribution even though Elev8 Seeds became the better-known commercial source for the seeds.

Its balanced hybrid classification also makes sense genetically. Neither side overwhelms the experience completely, and phenotypes can lean in different directions. Some emphasize citrus cream and an upbeat mental character; others bring more grape, earth, body relaxation, and density. That variation is part of what makes seed-grown examples interesting, particularly for cultivators hunting for a keeper rather than expecting every plant to duplicate one identical commercial clone.
Effects and Experience

The first portion of the 2 Scoops high tends to be socially friendly. Mood can rise quickly, conversation becomes easier, and familiar surroundings may take on a more entertaining quality. Rather than launching immediately into heavy sedation, the marijuana often begins with an enjoyable cerebral lift that can encourage talking, listening to music, watching a movie, gaming, or simply spending time with friends. Creative thinking may also become more fluid, although concentration can start to wander as the dose increases.

Physical relaxation develops underneath that brighter opening. A comfortable heaviness may spread through the limbs while mental tension gradually loses its urgency, giving this cannabis strain a balanced progression rather than a purely energetic or purely sedating experience. Appetite can become noticeably stronger as the high matures, which fits the strain’s dessert-like personality particularly well. Later in the session, larger amounts can turn the relaxed body sensation into substantial sleepiness.

Elev8 describes the potency of its seed release as “very high,” although it does not attach a standardized THC percentage to the cultivar. That distinction is important. THC concentration can vary significantly between phenotypes, cultivation environments, and harvests, so a specific laboratory number from one batch should not be treated as a universal figure for all 2 Scoops weed.
Medical Benefits

No clinical studies have evaluated 2 Scoops as an individual medical marijuana strain. Its reported combination of mood elevation, relaxation, and appetite stimulation may nevertheless interest cannabis consumers who prefer a hybrid that can ease into physical calm without beginning with immediate sedation. Temporary stress, low mood, mental fatigue, and difficulty unwinding are among the reasons someone might favor this general effect pattern.

As the body component becomes stronger, some consumers may also find the cultivar suitable for periods of physical tension, minor aches, loss of appetite, or difficulty settling down at night. Higher doses can shift the experience considerably toward rest, making the amount consumed as important as the strain itself.

Potent THC-rich marijuana is not universally calming. Excessive intake can cause anxiety, dizziness, dry mouth, impaired coordination, or an uncomfortable sense of mental heaviness. Anyone using cannabis for a medical condition should consider the laboratory analysis of the specific product and professional medical advice rather than relying only on the reputation associated with 2 Scoops.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Orange cream is the signature aroma. Elev8 compares the strain directly with old-school orange push pops and emphasizes that the sweetness is accompanied by noticeable funk. That combination gives the flower considerably more depth than its dessert-inspired name might suggest. Freshly opened buds can release creamy citrus first, followed by grape skins, berries, damp earth, and a pungent cannabis note underneath.

Grinding the flower tends to make the contrast stronger. Brighter orange and sugary fruit become more concentrated while peppery, earthy, or sour elements emerge from the interior of the bud. On inhalation, the flavor can resemble orange sherbet or citrus cream; the exhale often becomes darker, carrying grape, berry, and funky earth.

A definitive terpene hierarchy cannot be assigned to the original line because Elev8 does not publish a standardized laboratory terpene panel. Beta-caryophyllene, myrcene, limonene, and pinene would all be chemically plausible contributors to spicy, earthy, citrus, and herbal expressions, but actual dominance should be determined from a tested batch rather than inferred from flavor alone.
Growing Information

2 Scoops was released as a photoperiod hybrid in regular seed form, meaning growers could encounter both male and female plants rather than the feminized-only format common in many contemporary releases. Elev8 currently lists approximately nine weeks of flowering and describes production simply as “good.” Older descriptions of the line sometimes portrayed it as heavier yielding, but because the breeder does not provide a standardized grams-per-square-meter number, environmental conditions should be treated as the deciding factor.

Plant vigor is one of the cultivar’s useful characteristics. Healthy specimens can create sturdy branching capable of supporting chunky flowers, while the canopy generally responds well to topping or low-stress training. Giving the plant several strong primary branches before flowering can improve light distribution and reduce the risk of a single dominant top shading lower flower sites. A screen can also be useful when growers want to spread the canopy horizontally.

Trichome production becomes especially conspicuous late in bloom. Elev8 describes the flowers as heavily coated in frost, a characteristic that also appears repeatedly when the company uses 2 Scoops as breeding stock in later crosses. Dense resinous buds require good ventilation as flowering progresses, particularly where relative humidity remains high.

Outdoor timing has not been formally specified by the breeder. As a nine-week photoperiod cultivar, it would normally finish during autumn in the Northern Hemisphere, but exact harvest dates depend on latitude and when flowering begins. Warm, dry conditions late in the season are preferable because dense flower clusters become more vulnerable to moisture problems as they reach maturity.
FAQ
What are the genetics of 2 Scoops?

2 Scoops is Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet. It was originally created by T-Bud of T-Fly Genetics in Central California, with Elev8 Seeds later receiving permission to release the cultivar in seed form.
Is 2 Scoops indica or sativa?

It is best classified as a balanced indica/sativa hybrid. Individual plants may lean slightly toward one side, but the overall experience usually combines cerebral elevation with increasingly noticeable physical relaxation.
What does 2 Scoops taste like?

Creamy orange is the defining flavor, often compared with an orange push pop or orange sherbet. Grape, berries, sweetness, earth, and pungent funk develop underneath the citrus and give the strain a considerably richer finish.
How long does 2 Scoops take to flower?

Elev8 Seeds currently lists a flowering period of approximately nine weeks for its regular-seed release. Growers should still judge maturity from trichomes and flower development rather than harvesting automatically on a particular day.
Is 2 Scoops still available from Elev8 Seeds?

The original Elev8 Seeds release is currently listed as retired and out of stock. Flower or seeds carrying the name may still exist elsewhere, but their relationship to the original T-Fly selection should be confirmed when genetic authenticity matters.
Final Thoughts on 2 Scoops

2 Scoops works because its name accurately describes only the beginning of its personality. Grape Sherbet and Orange Sherbet provide the expected dessert foundation, but the finished weed adds substantial funk, resin, and potency to the equation. Creamy citrus can dominate the first impression before darker grape and earthy notes emerge, while the experience follows a similar progression from cheerful cerebral effects into a slower, heavier body state.

Its breeding history adds another reason for the cultivar to stand out. T-Bud of T-Fly Genetics regarded the selection highly enough that it became one of the genetics associated most strongly with his work, and Elev8 subsequently used 2 Scoops as breeding material in multiple later hybrids. For growers and cannabis enthusiasts interested in California dessert genetics, 2 Scoops offers more than sweetness: exceptional frost, strong aroma, balanced effects, and a distinctive orange-cream-and-funk profile give this retired hybrid an identity that remains easy to recognize.
